simple.meaning: אָח (ʼâch) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a fire-pot or chafing dish.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Jeremiah 36:22. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָח (H254) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אָח (ʼâch) / H254 is traced through Jeremiah 36:22, Jeremiah 36:23 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H254. ach II. אָח see II. אחח . II. אָח noun feminine fire-pot, brasier (Arabic in Thes, is an error) is loan-word from Egyptian &las— according to WMM OLZ 3, 51 ; Jer 36:22 read הָאָח וְאֵשׁ ; always with article 36:22 מְבֹעָ֑רֶת ׳הַא לְפָנָיו the brasier before him was burning ; 36:23 אֶלהָֿא אֲשֶׁר ׳הָאֵשׁ ; 36:23 עַלהָֿא אֲשֶׁר ׳הָאֵשׁ (I. אָח , brother see below אחה ; III. אָח interjection, p. 25).

occurrences.englishText: Now the king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month; and there was a fire in the brazier burning before him.
When Jehudi had read three or four leaves, the king cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was in the brazier, until all the scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the brazier.
